claim.quote: Λ-hypernuclei are produced and studied, with the FINUDA spectrometer, for the first time at an e+ e− collider: DAΦNE, the Frascati φ-factory.

date.locator: arXiv abstract page, submission date (arXiv:nucl-ex/0506028 v1, 30 June 2005)
date.note: arXiv submission date; published in Phys. Lett. B 622 (2005) 35.

key_value_text.quote: A preliminary analysis on 12 Λ C shows an energy resolution of 1.29 MeV FWHM on the hypernuclear levels, the best obtained so far with magnetic spectrometers at hadron facilities.
key_value_text.value: 12ΛC level spectrum with 1.29 MeV FWHM resolution (preliminary), the best obtained so far with magnetic spectrometers at hadron facilities

name: First Results on 12ΛC production at DAΦNE
notes: The Atlas keeps the arXiv v1 submission date; the abstract page text is the v3 listing.

summary.plain: FINUDA made and studied Λ-hypernuclei at an electron-positron collider for the first time, using slow kaons from phi-meson decays stopped in thin targets. A first look at carbon-12 hypernuclei gave a resolution of 1.29 MeV, the best so far for magnetic spectrometers at hadron facilities.
summary.technical: FINUDA at DAΦNE: first Λ-hypernuclear spectroscopy with K⁻ from φ decay stopped in thin targets (K⁻ stop + ᴬZ → ᴬΛZ + π⁻), from the first data taking (December 2003 to March 2004); preliminary analysis of 12ΛC gives 1.29 MeV FWHM resolution and capture rates for the ground and excited states (Phys. Lett. B 622 (2005) 35).

title: First Results on 12ΛC production at DAΦNE
why_it_matters: The abstract says the resolution is the best obtained so far with magnetic spectrometers at hadron facilities and that the study was made at an e+e- collider for the first time.
